short: A long reign in name only, with real power held first by his mother and then by the general Aetius.
full:
Valentinian III was installed as western emperor at Rome on 23 October 425 CE at the age of six, backed by eastern troops sent by his cousin Theodosius II, after a usurper had briefly held the throne. For over a decade his mother, Galla Placidia, governed as regent, and even after he came of age real military authority stayed with the general Flavius Aetius, who dominated the west for a generation.

Under this arrangement the western empire lost effective control of North Africa to the Vandals and much of Gaul and Spain to settled Gothic and other groups, while Aetius held what remained together. Valentinian, resentful of his general's power, killed Aetius with his own hands in 454 CE, only to be assassinated in turn by two of Aetius's former retainers on 16 March 455 CE, ending the Theodosian dynasty in the west.
